title: Mira and the Sunshine Cuddle Rock
markdown:
The Moonmallow Mountains are a most wonderfully gentle place, especially when the sun begins to tuck itself behind the sleepy peaks, painting the sky in soft shades of rose and lavender. In those quiet moments the air grows wonderfully mellow, carrying the sweet familiar scent of ripe berries and cool damp earth. And that is where Mira Pine liked to walk.

Mira Pine was a young witch, but not the kind who cackles or casts mischievous spells. She was the humming, meadow-wandering, quiet-adventure-seeking kind. Her little pointed hat, perched daintily on her head, was the colour of twilight lavender, a shade so soft it seemed to whisper secrets of the coming night. Her boots, made from the softest worn leather, made the most delightful thump-thump sounds as she ambled through the blackberry hollows. The plump blackberries hung like little purple jewels, heavy and glistening, just waiting for a sweet nibble. Mira loved the quiet peaceful hum of the hollow, the gentle whisper of the wind rustling through the broad green leaves, and the way the emerging moonlight began to paint everything in a pale silvery glow. It was a world of soft edges and gentle sounds.

As she hummed a little song, a tune she had made up herself about sleepy clouds drifting across a soft sky and fluffy sheep dozing in fields of clover, Mira heard a small tiny sound. It was not the rustle of a mouse in the undergrowth, nor the gentle chirp of a cricket. It was more like a little drawn-out sigh, a sound that seemed to melt into the quiet air. Hooo…

Curiosity, soft and gentle as a butterfly’s wing, fluttered in Mira’s chest. She peeked around a large mossy stone, its surface dappled with the fading sunlight. And there, curled up so tightly he looked like a warm little pebble, was a dragon. But oh, this dragon was ever so tiny. He was no bigger than Mira’s favourite, most cherished teacup, with scales that shimmered with the gentle flickering hues of a hearth fire just as it is about to settle into a peaceful sleep, all warm ember reds and soft oranges. His name, Mira somehow knew with a certainty as comforting as a warm hug, was Flicker. And Flicker looked very, very sleepy. His tiny eyelids were heavy, and his little snout was tucked neatly beneath his wing.

“Hello there.” Mira’s voice was as soft and light as a dandelion puff floating on a summer breeze.

Flicker blinked open his eyes, which were the colour of warm golden honey, liquid and sweet. “Hooo.” He stretched a little, unfolding one of his tiny ember-coloured wings, which unfurled like a delicate fan. “I am looking for a rock.”

Mira tilted her head, her lavender hat wobbling slightly with the movement. “A rock? What for, little Flicker?”

“For napping.” His voice was already thick with sleepiness. He let his little head droop towards the ground. “A perfect warm rock. My tummy feels all rumbley-empty for a nap, you see. But the ground, it is a little bit cool for my liking.” He gave another tiny wistful sigh. “I need a rock that feels like… like sunshine cuddles.”

Sunshine cuddles. That was what they needed.

Ah, sunshine cuddles. Now, Mira was a thoughtful child, and she pondered Flicker’s wish. It was a very important thing indeed, she thought. She smiled, a warm reassuring smile that reached her eyes. “I can help with that. I know all the best napping spots in the blackberry hollow.”

So, with the gentle promise of a cozy nap for Flicker, they began their search. It was a quiet unhurried expedition, a slow meandering through the dappled light. Mira, with her soft thump-thump boots, led the way, while Flicker followed with his tiny sleepy waddles, his little tail trailing behind him like a warm ember. They tiptoed past ferns that unfurled their delicate fronds like sleepy green wishes, and ducked under archways of brambles that were heavy with the weight of juicy ripe blackberries. The air around them smelled wonderfully sweet and earthy.

“How about this one?” Mira pointed to a round grey stone, worn smooth by the passing of many seasons, as smooth as a river pebble that had been tumbled and polished by flowing water.

Flicker curled his little tail around the stone and gave it a gentle pat with a tiny almost translucent claw. “Hmm. It is very nice, yes. It is smooth, and it is round. But it feels a little like a cool whisper against my scales, not sunshine cuddles at all.” And with that, he yawned again, a wide pink yawn that showed the very back of his tiny dragon throat.

They found another stone. This one was covered in a soft velvety carpet of emerald green moss. “This is comfy,” Flicker said, trying to snuggle into its yielding surface. But it was too soft. It felt like sinking into a damp cool blanket that had not quite dried properly. “This is too much like a puddle-snuggle. I need a rock. A proper solid rock.”

Mira looked from Flicker to the stones, then up at the leaves dancing above. The moon was still shy, and no stone seemed to offer that special warmth. She looked around the hollow, her kind eyes tracing the beautiful patterns the moonlight was beginning to weave through the leaves. She saw smooth stones, rough stones, tall stones that stood like sentinels, and short stones that lay almost hidden in the grass. But none of them seemed to radiate that special comforting warmth Flicker was searching for. None felt quite like sunshine cuddles.

“What about that one?” Flicker pointed with a tiny determined claw towards a little clearing, a small open space where the moonlight fell in a wide soft circle, as if the moon itself had chosen it as a special resting place. Nestled right in the middle of this luminous circle was a stone. It was not very big, perhaps only as large as Mira’s two hands put together, but it was wonderfully smooth, and it seemed to be almost glowing from within. Not with a bright dazzling light, but with a gentle inner glow, like a secret held safe. And around its base, growing in a little patch, was the most beautiful moss Mira had ever seen. It was the colour of a summer dawn, a delicate blend of pale pink and soft shimmering gold, and it seemed to be studded with tiny perfect droplets of dew that sparkled like miniature diamonds.

Mira, with her usual gentle grace, carefully reached out her hand towards the stone. As her fingers neared it, she felt its warmth. Oh, it was warm. Not hot, not burning, but a deep comforting warmth. It felt like holding a mug of warm milk on a chilly evening, or like a soft blanket wrapped around you on a cool night. It was the perfect true sunshine cuddle warmth.

“Flicker. I think I have found it. I think I have found your sunshine cuddle rock.”

Flicker wobbled over, his honey eyes wide and expectant. He gently, carefully, put one of his tiny paws onto the surface of the stone. A happy little rumble, a sound of pure contentment, vibrated through his small body. “Oh. It feels like a warm hug from a cloud. A very soft, very cozy cloud.”

Mira giggled, a soft musical sound. “That is exactly what sunshine cuddles feel like.”

She helped Flicker settle himself down onto the wonderfully warm stone. She carefully arranged his tiny wings, tucking them in just so, creating a small snug space for him. The luminous moss seemed to snuggle around him, like a soft glowing nest, embracing him in its gentle warmth. Flicker gave a contented sigh, a soft sleepy puff of warm air that smelled faintly of honey and dreams. His eyes, so full of sleepy searching just moments before, began to close, slowly and peacefully.

“Thank you, Mira Pine. This is the best rock. The very best sunshine cuddle rock in all the Moonmallow Mountains. It is perfect.”

Mira watched him for a moment, a warm happy feeling spreading through her own heart, as comforting and gentle as the moonlight itself. The little dragon was fast asleep, his tiny chest rising and falling with gentle peaceful breaths, his ember scales glowing softly in the moon’s pale light. The stone was warm beneath him, a perfect cradle, and the moon-moss glowed softly, like a lullaby made visible.

Mira whispered a soft farewell to Flicker, then turned to follow the shimmering moonbeams home. The blackberry hollow kept its quiet. The rock kept its warmth. Sunshine cuddles, after all.
characters: Mira Pine (young witch who hums meadow songs), Flicker (a teacup-sized dragon who wants sunshine cuddles)
